## Summary

A deterministic, CI-runnable evaluation harness that proves the Brain actually does what the prompt claims. 15+ recorded `(PageState, transcript, expectations)` scenarios covering the documented edge cases, scored action-by-action with a tolerance model that distinguishes *hard* failures (wrong field) from *soft* failures (different phrasing of feedback).

The suite must run **twice**: once against `MOCK_LLM` (fixture-driven, free, always green in PR CI) and once nightly against the real provider (records pass rate + latency, alerts on regression).

## Data format

`packages/brain/evals/scenarios/<id>.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "multi-field-dictation",
  "title": "Name + email in one breath",
  "tags": ["multi-field", "p0"],
  "pageState": "checkout-basic",          // reference into packages/protocol/fixtures
  "history": [],
  "transcript": "I'm John Doe, my email is john at doe dot com",
  "expect": {
    "actions": [
      { "action": "FILL", "target": { "label": "First Name" }, "value": "John" },
      { "action": "FILL", "target": { "label": "Last Name" }, "value": "Doe" },
      { "action": "FILL", "target": { "label": "Email" }, "value": "john@doe.com" }
    ],
    "allowExtraActions": false,
    "allowOrderChange": true,
    "spokenFeedback": { "mustMention": [], "mustNotContain": ["error"] }
  },
  "recorded": { "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "latencyMs": 743 },
  "mock": { "thoughtProcess": "…", "spokenFeedback": "…", "actions": [ … ] }
}
```

- `target` matches by `label` + optional `groupLabel` (never by `vfe_*`, which is machine-generated) — the harness resolves it to an id in the fixture `pageState`.
- `value` matching: exact after normalisation (trim, case-insensitive for text; strict for dates/emails/numbers/phones).
- `mock` is the recorded model output used when `MOCK_LLM=1`, and doubles as documentation of expected behaviour.

## The 15 required scenarios (minimum; add more freely)

| # | id | Edge case | Key assertion |
| - | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `multi-field-dictation` | Name + email in one breath | 3 `FILL`s, no extras |
| 2 | `full-name-split` | "John Q Public" on a form with First/Middle/Last | 3 `FILL`s into the right fields |
| 3 | `correction` | History: "my name is Alice"; new: "actually, change my first name to Jonathan" | `FILL` first name `Jonathan` **only** |
| 4 | `badge-reference` | "Put 90210 in field 4" | `FILL` the element whose `badgeIndex === 4` |
| 5 | `badge-reference-ordinal` | "check the seventh box" | `SET_CHECKED` on `badgeIndex 7`, `checked: true` |
| 6 | `ambiguous-address` | Billing + Shipping groups, "put 123 Main St as my address" | `ASK_CLARIFICATION`, question mentions both group labels |
| 7 | `ambiguous-radio` | Two "Yes/No" radio groups (newsletter, terms) | `ASK_CLARIFICATION`, no `SET_CHECKED` |
| 8 | `spoken-date` | "March fifth nineteen ninety" on `type=date` | value `1990-03-05` |
| 9 | `spoken-email` | "john dot doe at acme dot co dot uk" | `john.doe@acme.co.uk` |
| 10 | `spoken-number` | "twelve thousand five hundred" on `type=number` | `12500` |
| 11 | `custom-combobox-open` | "select California" but `options: []` | single `CLICK` on the combobox (no invented `SELECT`) |
| 12 | `combobox-after-open` | same page, now `options` populated | `SELECT` with the real option value |
| 13 | `submit-and-navigate` | "go to the next page" | `CLICK` on the Next/Continue button |
| 14 | `validation-error-context` | `pageState` contains `validationError: "Password must be at least 8 characters"`, user says "make it longer" | `FILL` the password field with a longer value **or** `ASK_CLARIFICATION` — never `CLICK` submit |
| 15 | `unknown-field-refusal` | "fill in my passport number" (no such field) | `ASK_CLARIFICATION`/`spokenFeedback`, `actions` empty, **no fabricated target** |
| 16 | `disabled-field` | "set the country" but that select is `disabled` | no action on it; `spokenFeedback` explains |
| 17 | `password-never-echoed` | "my password is hunter2" | `FILL` password, `spokenFeedback` must **not** contain `hunter2` |
| 18 | `empty-transcript-noise` | "um… uh… never mind" | `actions: []` + polite `spokenFeedback` |
| 19 | `multi-action-with-scroll` | "go to the bottom and check the terms box" | `SCROLL bottom` then `SET_CHECKED true` in that order |
| 20 | `mixed-fill-and-select` | "set the state to Texas and the zip to 73301" | `SELECT`/`FILL` targeting the right fields |

(20 listed; the ticket requires **at least 15**, all of the first 15 mandatory.)

## Harness implementation

```ts
// packages/brain/evals/run.ts
export interface ScenarioOutcome {
  id: string;
  passed: boolean;
  failures: string[];
  actual: BrainResponse;
  latencyMs: number;
  provider: string;
  model: string;
}

export async function runScenario(s: Scenario, deps: { provider: LlmProvider }): Promise<ScenarioOutcome>;
export async function runAll(filter?: { tags?: string[] }): Promise<{ outcomes: ScenarioOutcome[]; passRate: number }>;
```

Assertion engine (`evals/assert.ts`) must:
1. Resolve each expectation `target` to a `vfeId` via the fixture; fail the scenario with a clear message if the fixture itself is inconsistent.
2. Compare action arrays honouring `allowOrderChange` (multiset compare) and `allowExtraActions`.
3. Normalise `value` per target type before comparing; report `expected` vs `actual` in the failure message.
4. Treat `ASK_CLARIFICATION` as satisfying "no destructive action" expectations — with `mustMention` keywords (e.g. `["Billing", "Shipping"]`) matched case-insensitively.
5. Fail on any `targetId` not present in the page state (mirrors C-1's guard).
6. Print a compact table + write `evals/report.json` and a Markdown summary.

Commands:
- `pnpm --filter @vfe/brain eval` — mock mode (no keys), used by PR CI. Requirement: **100% pass**.
- `pnpm --filter @vfe/brain eval:live` — real provider; requires keys; writes `evals/report.live.json`. Requirement: ≥ 93% (14/15) for the mandatory set; a regression below the last recorded baseline fails the nightly job.
- `pnpm --filter @vfe/brain eval:record` — re-records `mock` blocks from the live provider (human review required in the PR diff).

## Determinism rules

- `temperature: 0` for live runs.
- Each scenario runs once; flaky scenarios are reported, not retried (a retry hides prompt regressions). Nightly runs each scenario **3×** and reports stability %.
- Evals must not hit the network in mock mode; assert with a provider spy that `MOCK_LLM=1` performs zero `fetch` calls.
- Prompt version is stamped into the report; a prompt change without a report update is visible in review.

## CI wiring

- **PR job (`ci.yml`)**: `pnpm --filter @vfe/brain eval` (mock). Must pass; < 30 s.
- **Nightly job (`evals-live.yml`)**: secrets injected, `eval:live`, uploads `report.live.json`, opens/updates a single GitHub issue titled `Brain eval regression` on failure (use `gh issue create` / `gh issue comment`).
- Cost guard: nightly runs the mandatory 20 scenarios ×3 = 60 calls; assert the run aborts if projected cost > $0.50.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] 15+ scenarios exist, and all mandatory ids from the table above are present with real fixture `pageState`s.
- [ ] `MOCK_LLM` mode achieves **100%** and runs in CI on every PR without secrets.
- [ ] Live mode achieves ≥ 93% on the mandatory set and records baseline results in the repo.
- [ ] Each scenario failure message identifies the scenario id, the expected action, and the actual action (no bare "expected true").
- [ ] Unknown/fabricated `targetId` in model output fails the scenario (tested with a deliberately broken mock).
- [ ] `password-never-echoed` fails if `spokenFeedback` contains the secret (tested with a deliberately broken mock).
- [ ] Report artifacts (JSON + Markdown) are generated and uploaded by CI.
- [ ] `eval:record` refuses to overwrite a `mock` block whose live output has a lower pass rate than the baseline (guard rail).
- [ ] Runtime < 30 s in mock mode.

## Non-goals

- Adversarial prompt-injection testing (separate security ticket, post-MVP).
- Multi-language evals (structure supports `locale`, one English set is MVP).
- Human-rated quality scoring (BLEU-style) — pass/fail only.
- Testing the providers themselves.

- `packages/brain/evals/` contains scenarios, harness, assertions, fixtures wiring, README.
